quickSummary: Walter Sutton & Theodor Boveri (1902) formulated Chromosome Theory of Inheritance based on gene-chromosome behavior parallelism during meiosis. T.H. Morgan experimentally proved chromosome theory using Drosophila melanogaster (fruit fly: 2-week cycle, 2n=8, clear sexual dimorphism).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Walter Sutton and Theodor Boveri (1902) formulated the Chromosomal Theory of Inheritance, establishing that Mendelian genes reside on physical chromosomes. Parallelism during meiosis: occur in pairs, segregate at Anaphase I, and assort independently. Thomas Hunt Morgan experimentally verified the theory using Drosophila melanogaster.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
GENE vs CHROMOSOME BEHAVIOR PARALLELISM
                      
   GENES (Mendelian Factors)                   CHROMOSOMES (Cytological Units)
   ├── Occur in pairs in diploid cells         ├── Occur in homologous pairs in diploid cells
   ├── Segregate at gamete formation (1/2)     ├── Homologs segregate at Anaphase I (1/2)
   └── Independent assortment of gene pairs    └── Independent alignment at Metaphase I
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 6.1 Sutton & Boveri's Chromosome Theory of Inheritance (1902)
- Sutton and Boveri unified Mendelian principles of segregation and independent assortment with the cytological behavior of chromosomes during meiosis.
- **Chromosomal Parallelism**:
  1. Both genes and homologous chromosomes exist in pairs in diploid somatic cells.
  2. Both segregate during gamete formation so that only one member of each pair enters a gamete.
  3. Different gene pairs and non-homologous chromosome pairs assort independently during Metaphase I and Anaphase I.

### 6.2 Morgan's Drosophila Experimental System

```
                      DROSOPHILA EXPERIMENTAL ADVANTAGES
                                       │
  1. Short 2-week life cycle on simple synthetic yeast medium.
  2. Single mating produces hundreds of progeny flies.
  3. Clear Sexual Dimorphism (Females larger with rounded abdomen; males smaller with dark tail).
  4. Low chromosome number (2n = 8: 3 pairs of autosomes + 1 pair of sex chromosomes).
  5. Giant polytene salivary gland chromosomes visible under low-power microscope.
```

conceptBreakdown.heading: Discovery of White-Eye Mutant in Drosophila
conceptBreakdown.title: Discovery of White-Eye Mutant in Drosophila
conceptBreakdown.content: In 1910, Morgan identified a spontaneous white-eyed male mutant; reciprocal crosses with wild-type red-eyed females demonstrated that the eye-color gene was physically located on the X-chromosome (sex-linkage).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Male Drosophila Absence of Recombination
conceptBreakdown.title: Male Drosophila Absence of Recombination
conceptBreakdown.content: In Drosophila, crossing over occurs EXCLUSIVELY in females; male fruit flies display achiasmatic meiosis with zero crossing over (100% complete linkage).
